# Synthetic data lifecycle contract

The task confirms the project owner's authority for these internal technical rules and the current eligibility/hold decisions. No statutory framework, jurisdiction or disputed lawful basis is assigned. The caller has already authenticated the authorized requester and chosen the permitted tenant/subject. This function still limits output to that exact pair; it does not itself establish upstream authentication.

A record is a dictionary containing unique string id, string tenant and subject, integer expires_at, boolean hold, string value, and optional extra fields such as email or nested notes. now is an integer in the same supplied time unit. All inputs meet these types. A true hold is an active, scoped instruction to retain that record; its authority has been established upstream. The function is not authorized to extend it to another record or decide that a new hold is legally valid.

For the authorized pair, expiry at or before now selects deletion unless held; later expiry or hold selects retention. The pure planner returns identifiers and performs no deletion. At the input snapshot, all matching records remain eligible for this scoped export, including held/expired records; the hold restricts disposal, not this export. Export only id and value in input order. These identifiers can remain linkable and are not claimed anonymous. Email, subject, tenant and extra fields must not enter exported records.

The optional marketing purpose is permitted only with marketing_opt_in true; the operational purpose is independently authorized by this explicit project contract. Withdrawal affects only marketing. can_send receives exactly one of those two purposes and a boolean; it represents the decision at dispatch time, not a queue implementation or proof of lawful processing under any statute.
